transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Alex Gomez (Redwood SE), Evan Torres (Blue Marlin Head of ML), Priya Singh (Blue Marlin VP Eng), Liam O'Connor (Blue Marlin SRE), Nora Diaz (Blue Marlin Finance)

Auto-generated summary (optional):
- Quick health check: usage spike last week, 3x baseline around marketing event.
- Cost and latency tradeoffs discussed; customer leaning toward dedicated pool with canary fallback to hosted.
- Action: run pilot benchmark, share cost model and SOC2 + network docs.

Topics: usage spike, right-sizing Dedicated, latency targets, security & compliance (SOC 2 / KMS), pilot plan, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call - Jordan here, Samira, Priya from my side. Hey Evan, Priya, Liam, Nora?
[00:08] Evan Torres: Yep here, thanks. Sorry for the slight delay, had to push through a standup.
[00:12] Priya Singh: All good, excited to dig in.
[00:14] Samira Patel: Awesome. So agenda — short health, dig into the spike last week, then rightsize options and pilot details. We should leave time for questions on security.
[00:25] Evan Torres: That sounds good. Quick datapoint — we saw a 3x token volume spike for three hours during the campaign, p95 latency climbed from 150ms to about 420ms. p99 hit 1.1s. CPU/GPU utilization basically saturated on our dedicated instance.
[00:40] Liam O'Connor: Yeah and we had a couple of timeouts from the mobile clients; we retried and served from cache for some endpoints. Not catastrophic but enough to trigger pager.
[00:50] Jordan Lee: Got it. thanks for that. did you run anything against the new quantized variant we recommended?
[00:56] Evan Torres: We did a small baseline last month but the campaign used the default highest-fidelity model, not the quantized one. we hesitated because of regen quality concerns.
[01:06] Samira Patel: Right — common tradeoff. we can show you expected latency/cost delta for the quantized variant vs the full fp32/16 run. Also batching and prefix cache improvements should reduce tokens served per request.
[01:20] Priya Singh: On quality — our product team measured hallucination rates and there was a small uptick with the 4-bit quantized candidate, but for the campaign responses the acceptance criteria was lower, so it might have been acceptable. we need a clearer eval run.
[01:35] Jordan Lee: Understood. For right-sizing there are a few levers: (1) Dedicated capacity sizing, (2) autoscale/burst policy, (3) smart routing to hosted fallback, and (4) quantization + batching. We can show a recommended config that meets your p95 250ms target at 99% at an X% cost delta — we'll put numbers in the cost model.
[01:56] Nora Diaz: We care about cost — show me the delta in actual dollars. Marketing wants predictable invoicing, so spikes need containment or a burst pool.
[02:05] Samira Patel: We recommend reserved baseline + burst buffer. burst buffer can be billed at a higher nominal rate but it prevents client-facing errors. we can model a monthly burnline and a surge charge estimate.
[02:18] Evan Torres: Can Redwood guarantee a fallback to hosted if our dedicated pool fills up? we need graceful degradation not full outage.
[02:25] Alex Gomez: Yes — smart routing policy can fall back to a compatible hosted model variant. functionally it's a config: you choose the tolerance for increased latency or cost. It isn't a hard SLA unless you buy a specific plan, but it will keep traffic flowing.
[02:37] Priya Singh: We also need audit logs for every token event — our compliance team needs per-request tracing for a sample set.
[02:45] Priya Nair: We can provide token-level tracing and per-route logs; retention and redaction are configurable. we'll share our audit coverage doc.
[02:55] Liam O'Connor: On the private deployment side — we want VPC peering and KMS integration. network egress must stay internal. Any gotchas?
[03:04] Samira Patel: Private deployment supports VPC with customer-managed peering and KMS/HSM integration. common snag: need IAM role for the peering host and KMS grant for Redwood's service principal. We'll include a checklist.
[03:18] Evan Torres: Sounds good. what about SOC2 scope? we have an upcoming audit in Q3 and need clear evidence.
[03:24] Jordan Lee: Redwood's SOC 2 Type II is available; we'll send the report and a mapping guide for control evidence. For on-prem or private, some attestations differ but we'll call those out.
[03:33] Nora Diaz: Finance question — can you show committed reserved capacity pricing vs on-demand? also any discounts for annual?
[03:40] Jordan Lee: Yes, reserved monthly/annual contracts exist and we can run multiple tiers. I'll send a plan comparison with monthly burn and effective per-token costs for your mix.
[03:49] Priya Singh: For the pilot, we want a two-week run with our staging traffic plus a synthetic 30% surge. can Redwood run the benchmark and produce a headroom plan?
[03:58] Samira Patel: Absolutely. we'll need a 7-day trace and representative prompt sets. We will run across quantized and baseline models and with different batching settings. We'll include KV/prefix cache enabled vs disabled.
[04:12] Evan Torres: We'll provide the trace. also need the pilot to exercise our multi-tenant routing since multiple product teams will be hitting the same endpoints.
[04:21] Alex Gomez: Note: multi-tenant routing means we should test per-tenant rate limiting and the token-level quota. we'll include that in the runner.
[04:29] Priya Nair: Question from our product team — what's the expected p95 improvement if you enable prefix KV caching and continuous batching?
[04:36] Samira Patel: Conservative estimate: 20-35% p95 improvement for repeat prefix-heavy workloads; cost-per-token can drop by ~18-30% depending on cache hit rate. we'll validate with your traces.
[04:48] Liam O'Connor: There was some confusion on our side about the fallback model family — will fallbacks keep the same instruction/response shape or will we need translation layers?
[04:57] Alex Gomez: We map by model compatibility. usually the hosted fallback is a smaller-capacity but functionally compatible model. for function/tool calling we keep the same interface; minor prompt templating adjustments might be needed in edge cases.
[05:11] Evan Torres: Any limitations on quantization for function calling or streaming? we rely on streaming for mobile UX.
[05:18] Samira Patel: Streaming is supported by quantized variants, but some very aggressive quantizations can increase tokenization noise; we'll recommend a validated quant profile that keeps streaming behavior intact.
[05:30] Priya Singh: Ok let's recap — we want: (1) cost model with reserved vs burst pricing, (2) pilot benchmark schedule + runner, (3) SOC2 and private deployment checklist, (4) recommended quant/batching config and expected p95/p99 numbers.
[05:45] Jordan Lee: Agreed. I'll own the cost model. Samira will own the benchmark runner. Evan to provide traces. Liam to configure staging network.
[05:54] Nora Diaz: timeline: can we have the cost model and SOC docs by Monday? finance wants next-week review.
[06:00] Jordan Lee: Yes — cost model and SOC + network checklist by 2026-04-12. Samira will aim to have the runner ready and a pilot kickoff slot the week of 2026-04-20.
[06:10] Evan Torres: Perfect. Also quick heads up — competitor benchmarking: we're also talking to Anthropic about managed endpoints; would be useful if Redwood could include a line-item comparison.
[06:20] Jordan Lee: we'll include competitor notes at a high level — pricing and feature delta.
[06:24] Priya Singh: One last ops question — during the spike, our telemetry showed single-tenant starvation where one tenant consumed most of the burst. can we enforce per-tenant caps?
[06:34] Alex Gomez: Yes — per-tenant quotas, circuit-breakers, and token-level throttling are available. we can propose soft-limits plus a backpressure strategy.
[06:45] Evan Torres: cool. that should reduce blast radius.
[06:47] Jordan Lee: Great. we'll follow up with the artifacts. thanks everyone for the time.
[06:53] Priya Nair: thanks, talk soon.
[06:55] (call ends)

Post-meeting notes:
- Customer requested a pilot to run with staging VPC peering.
- Priority: cost model for finance review, SOC2 artifacts, and benchmark runner.
- Risk: customer may pursue Anthropic pilots in parallel; Redwood should emphasize the integration checklist and expected headroom numbers.
